columns.title: Spatial resolution
columns.subtitle: Grid spacing & support
columns.definition: The spacing of the output grid, and the area each value represents. A fine output grid does not by itself establish the scale of credible information.

topics.title: Annual precipitation
topics.intro: Evaluate totals over the area and year definition used in your water balance. Start with seasonal and annual performance before selecting a finer output grid.

figure.title: The same annual total can hide a different season.
figure.alt: Two synthetic monthly precipitation series both total 960 mm, but one has winter peaks and the other is constant.
figure.caption: Both constructed examples total 960 mm in one year. The first has a winter maximum; the second has 80 mm each month. Annual agreement alone cannot establish seasonal agreement.
figure.provenance: Original synthetic example, generated with Matplotlib. No observations or downscaling product output are shown.

cells.title: Catchment spatial support
cells.summary: Choose a spatial scale that represents your catchment and elevation gradients. Fine grid spacing is not a guarantee of accurate basin totals.
cells.body:
Choose a spatial scale that represents your catchment and elevation gradients. Fine grid spacing is not a guarantee of accurate basin totals.

## Evaluation check

Compare area-weighted annual totals and elevation bands with an appropriate reference. Record the regridding method.

## Basin aggregation

For grid-cell precipitation $P_i$ and overlapping basin areas $A_i$, the area-weighted mean is

$$
\bar{P} = \frac{\sum_i A_i P_i}{\sum_i A_i}.
$$

Use consistent units and account for cells with missing values. This equation defines the aggregation, not product skill.

![Synthetic monthly totals illustrating why seasonal evaluation matters](/content-assets/guidance/figures/annual-precipitation.png)

_Illustrative synthetic data, not observations or a product benchmark. See the application figure for provenance._

cells.title: Annual aggregation
cells.summary: Monthly or daily accumulations can support annual totals when the record is complete. Subdaily output is not required for this statistic alone.
cells.body:
Monthly or daily accumulations can support annual totals when the record is complete. Subdaily output is not required for this statistic alone.

## Evaluation check

Check precipitation units, calendar, missing intervals, and whether your target uses calendar years or water years.

cells.title: Climate model uncertainty
cells.summary: Use several driving models to examine uncertainty in projected annual changes. A large file count may still represent only a few models.

evidence.statement: Lehner et al. used seven single-model large ensembles alongside CMIP5 and CMIP6 to distinguish internal variability from model-response uncertainty.
evidence.scope: Global and regional temperature and precipitation projections; not a downscaled product comparison.

cells.body:
Use several driving models to examine uncertainty in projected annual changes. A large file count may still represent only a few models.

## Evaluation check

Report model identities, scenario, and the distribution of basin-scale changes. Keep model and member counts separate.

cells.title: Forced change and internal variability
cells.summary: For short records or modest changes, internal variability can affect the interpretation of annual precipitation trends.

evidence.statement: Uncertainty partitioning based on a single realization can be biased at regional scales; the study obtained more accurate separation using multiple initial-condition large ensembles.
evidence.scope: Results depend on the region, variable, and ensemble archive considered.

cells.body:
For short records or modest changes, internal variability can affect the interpretation of annual precipitation trends.

## Evaluation check

Compare changes across initial-condition members where available. Keep the same baseline and future window.

cells.title: Include the full basin
cells.summary: Check that the product covers the entire contributing area, including upstream regions across national boundaries.
cells.body:
Check that the product covers the entire contributing area, including upstream regions across national boundaries.

## Evaluation check

Overlay the product mask and basin boundary. Quantify the fraction of basin area without valid coverage.

cells.title: Baseline and future periods
cells.summary: Require a usable historical reference period and output covering the planning horizon and scenario of interest.
cells.body:
Require a usable historical reference period and output covering the planning horizon and scenario of interest.

## Evaluation check

Inventory years, calendars, scenario transitions, and missing periods before comparing climatologies.

topics.title: Annual maximum precipitation
topics.intro: Define the accumulation duration and spatial support first. A maximum hourly point value, a maximum daily grid value, and a basin-average storm maximum answer different questions.

figure.title: A daily total does not identify an hourly peak.
figure.alt: Two synthetic 24-hour storms both total 48 mm. One is steady at 2 mm each hour; the other places all 48 mm in two hours with a peak of 30 mm.
figure.caption: The constructed storms have identical daily accumulations of 48 mm and different hourly maxima. Daily output alone cannot distinguish these within-day sequences.
figure.provenance: Original synthetic example, generated with Matplotlib. No observations or downscaling product output are shown.

cells.title: Resolve the event scale
cells.summary: Check extremes at the footprint your application uses. Fine grids can still inherit unresolved storm processes or unsuitable spatial dependence.
cells.body:
Check extremes at the footprint your application uses. Fine grids can still inherit unresolved storm processes or unsuitable spatial dependence.

## Evaluation check

Evaluate maxima after aggregating both product and reference to the same area. Separate point and areal targets.

cells.title: Match the duration
cells.summary: Daily data cannot directly supply hourly extremes. The output interval must resolve your target accumulation duration.
cells.body:
Daily data cannot directly supply hourly extremes. The output interval must resolve your target accumulation duration.

## Evaluation check

Check fixed versus rolling windows, timestamp conventions, and whether temporal disaggregation has been independently evaluated.

cells.title: Compare tail changes
cells.summary: Examine how annual maxima and their projected changes differ across driving models and downscaling choices.
cells.body:
Examine how annual maxima and their projected changes differ across driving models and downscaling choices.

## Evaluation check

Compare duration-specific maxima using the same period, region, scenario, and estimator across models.

cells.title: Sample rare events
cells.summary: Annual maxima are noisy. Initial-condition ensembles help assess how much an extreme estimate depends on the realized climate sequence.

evidence.statement: Bhatia and Ganguly found that concatenating initial-condition ensemble information reduced uncertainty in precipitation-extreme estimates and depth-duration-frequency curves in their analysis.
evidence.scope: CESM large-ensemble experiment; pooling requires the assumptions and climate windows to be appropriate.

cells.body:
Annual maxima are noisy. Initial-condition ensembles help assess how much an extreme estimate depends on the realized climate sequence.

## Evaluation check

Report record length and member count alongside interval estimates. Do not pool unequal climates as one stationary sample.

cells.title: Capture storm footprints
cells.summary: Large-area flood studies need complete storm coverage. A small site study may need a smaller domain, but still needs credible regional processes.
cells.body:
Large-area flood studies need complete storm coverage. A small site study may need a smaller domain, but still needs credible regional processes.

## Evaluation check

Check storm coverage, coastlines, mountain regions, and proximity to a regional model boundary.

cells.title: Record length for extremes
cells.summary: Short time slices supply few annual maxima. Extrapolated return levels require uncertainty estimates and explicit climate assumptions.
cells.body:
Short time slices supply few annual maxima. Extrapolated return levels require uncertainty estimates and explicit climate assumptions.

## Evaluation check

State the years and missing-year rule. Show sensitivity to fitting window, distribution, and nonstationarity assumptions.

topics.title: Intermittency
topics.intro: Define a wet interval before counting wet days or spells. Then evaluate both occurrence and persistence. Matching the precipitation distribution does not establish that the sequence is useful.

figure.title: Wet frequency does not identify spell length.
figure.alt: Two constructed 12-day rainfall sequences contain six wet days and 12 mm total. One alternates wet and dry days; the other groups six wet days together.
figure.caption: Both sequences have six wet days and 12 mm of precipitation. At a threshold of 1 mm/day, the longest dry spell within the displayed window is one day in the alternating sequence and six days in the clustered sequence.
figure.provenance: Original synthetic example, generated with Matplotlib. No observations or downscaling product output are shown.

cells.title: Wet-interval definition
cells.summary: A catchment can receive rain somewhere while one location remains dry. Occurrence depends on spatial aggregation.
cells.body:
A catchment can receive rain somewhere while one location remains dry. Occurrence depends on spatial aggregation.

## Evaluation check

Compute wet frequency and spells at the station, grid, or basin support used in the application.

cells.title: Preserve the sequence
cells.summary: Use a timestep suited to the dry or wet spells you need. Monthly totals do not identify consecutive dry days.

evidence.statement: Lange evaluated dry-day frequency separately from wet-day intensity, defining dry days using a precipitation threshold of 0.1 mm/day.
evidence.scope: ISIMIP3BASD v1.0 evaluation; this threshold is a study definition, not a universal application threshold.

cells.body:
Use a timestep suited to the dry or wet spells you need. Monthly totals do not identify consecutive dry days.

## Evaluation check

Check dry-spell lengths, wet-spell lengths, and wet-to-wet transition frequency using a documented threshold.

cells.title: Compare occurrence
cells.summary: Assess whether driving models and downscaling methods give consistent changes in wet frequency and spell persistence.
cells.body:
Assess whether driving models and downscaling methods give consistent changes in wet frequency and spell persistence.

## Evaluation check

Compare occurrence and persistence separately from wet-day intensity across the available models.

cells.title: Sample long spells
cells.summary: A single realization may include too few persistent dry or wet events for your intended risk estimate.
cells.body:
A single realization may include too few persistent dry or wet events for your intended risk estimate.

## Evaluation check

Examine the variability of longest spells across years and members. Report sample size and uncertainty.

cells.title: Follow regional spells
cells.summary: Regional drought applications need consistent occurrence across the whole study area. Point applications may not need a continental domain.
cells.body:
Regional drought applications need consistent occurrence across the whole study area. Point applications may not need a continental domain.

## Evaluation check

Measure simultaneous dry conditions across subregions rather than relying only on individual grid-cell metrics.

cells.title: Sequence completeness
cells.summary: Missing intervals and disconnected time slices can truncate spells or create false ones.
cells.body:
Missing intervals and disconnected time slices can truncate spells or create false ones.

## Evaluation check

Retain missingness, verify continuity, and define how spells crossing year or scenario boundaries are handled.

topics.title: Precipitation phase
topics.intro: Total precipitation alone does not identify phase. Establish whether rain and snow are provided directly or diagnosed from other variables, and evaluate the partitioning method.

figure.title: The assumed transition changes the rain fraction.
figure.alt: Two illustrative sigmoid curves show different rain fractions at the same air temperature when the assumed transition midpoint shifts from 0 to 2 degrees Celsius.
figure.caption: These logistic curves are mathematical illustrations with chosen transition midpoints of 0 and 2 degrees Celsius and slope scale 0.8 degrees Celsius. They are not fitted phase models or recommended thresholds. See Jennings et al. below for observational evidence.
figure.provenance: Original synthetic example, generated with Matplotlib. No observations or downscaling product output are shown.

cells.title: Represent elevation
cells.summary: Assess terrain and elevation differences between the product, observations, and impact model before using rain-snow partitioning.

evidence.statement: Across 95% of the observed stations, the temperature associated with equal rain and snow frequency ranged from -0.4 to 2.4 degrees Celsius.
evidence.scope: Northern Hemisphere station observations over 29 years; these are transition statistics, not recommended fixed thresholds.

cells.body:
Assess terrain and elevation differences between the product, observations, and impact model before using rain-snow partitioning.

## Evaluation check

Check elevation-band rain fractions and snow accumulation. Document any lapse-rate or terrain adjustment.

cells.title: Pair weather variables
cells.summary: Check that precipitation and the variables used to diagnose phase refer to compatible times and locations.

evidence.statement: Phase methods incorporating humidity performed better than air-temperature-only methods in the conditions evaluated by Jennings et al.
evidence.scope: Improvement was especially evident below saturation and at air temperatures between 0.6 and 3.4 degrees Celsius.

cells.body:
Check that precipitation and the variables used to diagnose phase refer to compatible times and locations.

## Evaluation check

Inspect available rain, snowfall, temperature, and humidity variables. Test phase estimates at the application timestep.

cells.title: Compare phase response
cells.summary: Snow-related impacts depend on the joint changes in temperature and precipitation across models.
cells.body:
Snow-related impacts depend on the joint changes in temperature and precipitation across models.

## Evaluation check

Compare rain fraction and seasonal snowfall changes, not just changes in total precipitation.

cells.title: Sample snow seasons
cells.summary: Consider member variability when estimating the frequency of low-snow years or rain-on-snow conditions.
cells.body:
Consider member variability when estimating the frequency of low-snow years or rain-on-snow conditions.

## Evaluation check

Compare event and seasonal metrics across available members without treating members as distinct climate models.

cells.title: Cover the snow zone
cells.summary: The footprint must include the elevations contributing snow storage and meltwater to the study area.
cells.body:
The footprint must include the elevations contributing snow storage and meltwater to the study area.

## Evaluation check

Check mountain coverage, product masks, and the observation network supporting evaluation.

cells.title: Seasonal phase changes
cells.summary: Use historical and future windows that support evaluation of the changing snowfall season.
cells.body:
Use historical and future windows that support evaluation of the changing snowfall season.

## Evaluation check

Check seasonal completeness and scenario availability. Compare phase by month and elevation, not just annually.

topics.title: Spatial coherence
topics.intro: Evaluate whether precipitation occurs together at different locations. Good individual grid-cell distributions do not establish credible storm footprints or basin-average extremes.

figure.title: The same local values can produce a different basin peak.
figure.alt: Synthetic rainfall at two equal-area cells has the same distribution in each cell in both cases. Synchronized rain gives a basin maximum of 20 mm/day; staggered rain gives a maximum of 10 mm/day.
figure.caption: Each cell has the same set of daily values in both examples. Changing the relative timing changes the equal-area basin mean and its maximum. This is a constructed dependence example, not an evaluation of a named product.
figure.provenance: Original synthetic example, generated with Matplotlib. No observations or downscaling product output are shown.

cells.title: Spatial dependence
cells.summary: Spatial dependence must be evaluated directly. A high-resolution grid alone does not establish coherent precipitation fields.

evidence.statement: Spatial variability was poorly represented by almost all methods participating in the VALUE perfect-predictor experiment.
evidence.scope: Present-climate evaluation of the participating methods; it does not establish performance for all methods or future climates.

cells.body:
Spatial dependence must be evaluated directly. A high-resolution grid alone does not establish coherent precipitation fields.

## Evaluation check

Compare correlation with distance, simultaneous extremes, and basin-average event totals at common spatial support.

cells.title: Check synchronized storms
cells.summary: Use synchronized timestamps and an interval that resolves the propagation or concurrence of events of interest.
cells.body:
Use synchronized timestamps and an interval that resolves the propagation or concurrence of events of interest.

## Evaluation check

Inspect event maps and time sequences. Check temporal disaggregation for independent timing across neighboring cells.

cells.title: Test each method
cells.summary: Assess field behavior across driving models and downscaling methods before treating them as interchangeable.
cells.body:
Assess field behavior across driving models and downscaling methods before treating them as interchangeable.

## Evaluation check

Apply the same spatial dependence diagnostics to each product version and driving model.

cells.title: Sample joint extremes
cells.summary: More members can provide more regional events, but cannot repair a method that misrepresents spatial dependence.
cells.body:
More members can provide more regional events, but cannot repair a method that misrepresents spatial dependence.

## Evaluation check

Evaluate dependence first, then estimate uncertainty in regional event metrics across members.

cells.title: Use a continuous field
cells.summary: Require spatially consistent coverage across connected catchments or assets. Inspect seams when combining products.
cells.body:
Require spatially consistent coverage across connected catchments or assets. Inspect seams when combining products.

## Evaluation check

Check overlap, masks, boundary behavior, and simultaneous precipitation across the full application domain.

cells.title: Keep comparable events
cells.summary: Use overlapping periods and compatible calendars for spatial diagnostics. Avoid comparing different seasons or unmatched event records.
cells.body:
Use overlapping periods and compatible calendars for spatial diagnostics. Avoid comparing different seasons or unmatched event records.

## Evaluation check

For free-running climate simulations, compare event statistics rather than requiring storms on observed dates.

kendon.journal: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
kendon.support: The reviewed convection-permitting simulations improve several subdaily rainfall characteristics. That finding does not imply uniform improvements in daily means, or make grid spacing alone a skill measure.
kendon.scope: Regional convection-permitting modeling evidence. Applicability depends on location, process, and configuration.

lange.title: Trend-preserving bias adjustment and statistical downscaling with ISIMIP3BASD (v1.0)
lange.support: This method separates bias adjustment from spatial downscaling and explicitly handles dry-day frequency. Its evaluation illustrates why trend preservation and spatial variability need their own checks.
lange.scope: Evidence about ISIMIP3BASD v1.0. It does not establish the behavior of every bias-adjusted product.

lehner.title: Partitioning climate projection uncertainty with multiple large ensembles and CMIP5/6
lehner.support: Multiple single-model ensembles help separate internal variability from differences in model response. The study shows why those uncertainty sources need separate treatment at regional scales.
lehner.scope: Climate-model uncertainty analysis; not a downscaled product ranking.

maraun.title: Bias Correction, Quantile Mapping, and Downscaling: Revisiting the Inflation Issue
maraun.support: Using quantile mapping to bridge mismatched spatial scales can misrepresent dependence and area-mean extremes. Matching local distributions is therefore insufficient evidence of credible regional precipitation.

guidance.title: LOCA2 North America evaluation guidance
guidance.summary: Provisional application guidance; evaluate the selected product release.
guidance.body:
## Application guidance

Treat LOCA2 as a candidate for basin water-balance and daily precipitation studies. Evaluate basin totals, wet/dry spells, and spatial dependence at the scale used by the application. Fine grid spacing alone does not demonstrate suitability.

## Version and evaluation checks

Record the precipitation release and the model/member/scenario combination. The provider reports a precipitation update in September 2024. Do not transfer an evaluation of an older release to a new one without checking the changes.

The ensemble study is documented in [Pierce et al. (2023)](https://cirrus.ucsd.edu/~pierce/papers/Pierce_et_al_JHM_2023_LOCA2_precip_extremes_VoR.pdf). Compare extremes over matched accumulation windows and quantify sampling uncertainty. Daily data alone cannot provide hourly intensity-duration-frequency estimates.

## Expert contribution needed

Add regional evaluation results, diagnostics, and evidence of limitations here. State the product release, basin, reference data, period, and application. These suggestions are an AI-assisted draft and have not been endorsed by a domain expert.

Use member-level series to estimate internal variability while keeping results grouped by parent GCM. Compare balanced parent-model summaries with any pooled-member result.

## Application guidance

Compare basin and elevation-band precipitation against independent observations where possible. Record the processed GMET reference used in training and do not treat it as independent validation.

## Interpretation limits

The cap described in [Hartke et al. (2024)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-024-04205-z) applies to the training observations. Check the actual output distribution rather than assuming a 500 mm/day ceiling in the projections. Preserve parent-model identity when pooling members. All three parent models have relatively high climate sensitivity, and the archive samples only SSP3-7.0.
